text:
Alex: heads-up — after the kernel-selector switch (PR #3421) I'm seeing a ~8-12ms p99 increase for short sequences (<=64) on the host path. looks like host-side overheads are now the dominant tail.

Maria: saw perf dash spike this morning, good catch. can you paste the short flame / profiler snapshot?

Alex: pasted a trimmed flame below — this is aggregated per-request p99 from a canary run
```
host_total: 52ms
  parse/ingress: 22ms
    http2/frame_parse: 10ms
    tokenize (utf8->ids): 9ms
    header/validation: 3ms
  kvcache/lookup: 6ms
  batching/route: 3ms
  runtime/dispatch: 14ms
```

Vikram: interesting — tokenize + http2 frame parsing are almost half the p99. kernel selector change shouldn't touch tokenization. did selector change cause more small-batch fallsbacks? that would increase per-request scheduling overhead and expose host costs.

Alex: I measured batching sizes — mean batch size for these short seqs dropped from 4.1 -> 1.9 after the switch. so yes, more single-request decode paths.

Maria: KV hit-rate for these traces? if KV miss climbs we also pay decode + kernel startup often.

Alex: kvcache hit-rate for affected workload fell from 93% -> 82% in the canary window. metric correlates with requests that had small batch sizes.

Jen SRE: @Vikram @Alex let's triage quickly. hypothesis: kernel-selector heuristics prefer a lower-latency kernel that has worse startup for tiny batches -> causes backpressure on prefix caching and reduces coalescing.

Vikram: action items:
- add microbenchmark: kernel warmup cost for batch sizes 1..8 (Vikram)
- add quick patch: force batch-threshold >= 3 for selector when seq_len <= 64 (Alex)
- profile ingress parsing path under single-request decode (Maria)

IngressBot: deploy canary 2026-03-20T09:12Z triggered: rollback-flag=off, selector=canary-3421

Alex: quick patch (+toggle) turned p99 down ~6ms on canary. still want the kernel warmup numbers before deciding permanent fix.

Maria: I'll capture a tcpdump + http2 frames for a few requests to see if frame fragmentation changed; also verifying writev coalescing on host socket.

Vikram: if kernel warmup is the issue we should consider: pre-kernel-selection warm-up for small batches, or prefer a slightly higher-latency per-token kernel that has lower startup cost. also consider making batching heuristics more tolerant (prefer >=2 coalesce) for ingress.

Jen SRE: please file a follow-up with perf numbers + rolling plan. assign to eng-runtime epic: HOST-OVHD-2026. I'll monitor canary and slow-roll if green :thumbsup:

Alex: filing ticket now and attaching traces. thanks all.
